messages:
emma: Heads-up — Borealis customer LoRA shows weird 'token shadowing' after merge + int4: two visually-identical tokens map to different ids, causing duplicated/garbled vendor fields in NER extraction.

raj: Interesting. Not the usual spm build mismatch?

emma: Not exactly. Found Unicode normalization differences. Finetune data normalized with NFKC, base vocab was built with NFC. So e.g. 'Cömpany' (o + diaeresis as combining) vs 'Cömpany' (precomposed) end up as separate token surfaces. Merge leaves both forms present; quant/packing amplifies the mismatch.

carmen: Oof. That explains why remap-by-token-surface fails sometimes — surface looks the same visually to humans but encodes differently. Any quick repro?

emma: Quick repro: `python eval_pack/run_eval.py --pack borealis_ner_150 --model merged_borealis_lora --quant int4`

emma: Example snippet:
INPUT: "Vendor: Cömpany A
Amount: $42.00"
FP16: "Vendor: Cömpany A"
INT4: "Vendor: Cömpany A" (wrong form leads to split/unk)

raj: So we need normalization-aware remap. Two options: (1) force-normalize finetune tokenizer artifact to base Unicode form prior to merge (retokenize or rebase), or (2) build a canonicalization table that maps equivalent unicode decompositions to a single base id at merge time. Option (2) seems faster and reversible.

carmen: Agreed. Also watch out for collisions — mapping decomposed->composed may collide with existing token ids. We'll need to patch embedding rows and any quant-block metadata.

emma: I built a prototype: `tools/tokenmap/normalize_rebase.py --lora lora_borealis.pt --canon NFC --out lora_borealis_nfcrebase.pt`. It canonicalizes token surfaces then reindexes deltas. Can @eval-bot run borealis_ner_150 comparing fp16, int4_raw, int4_nfcrebase?

eval-bot: queued run 5512347905: borealis_ner_150 on merged_borealis fp16,int4_raw,int4_nfcrebase. ETA ~7m.

devops-bot: FYI: when reindexing, ensure checksum of quant-block metadata updated in artifact manifest.

raj: Interim numbers from staging: fp16 F1=0.88, int4_raw F1=0.54, int4_nfcrebase F1=0.83. Normalization rebase recovers majority. A small residual 3% gap due to ambiguous ligatures and some customer-provided glyph variants that were normalized inconsistently in their dataset.

carmen: For those residuals we can offer a lightweight calibration: run a 2-5 minute constrained fine-tune on remapped ids using a small heldout set (20-40 customer samples) to nudge LoRA deltas. That helped in similar cases.

emma: Proposed actions: 1) add unicode-normalization check into LoRA merge CI and warn/block if mismatch unless `--allow-normalize` given, 2) include normalization-rebase tool in merge pipeline (default NFC canonicalization), 3) offer optional quick-calibrate step `--calibrate-heldout` for customer samples, 4) add 30-sample adversarial subset to borealis_ner pack containing decomposed/composed variants. I'll open PR with repro commands, the prototype script, and staging run id 5512347905.

raj: :thumbsup: Also add a note to onboarding checklist for SEs: "confirm unicode normalization used during finetune".

carmen: I'll add unit tests for canonicalization collisions and update the remap tool to patch quant-block headers.

emma: Thanks all — will file the PR and tag infra for a follow-up run that includes calibration. If anyone wants to re-run comparisons (retokenize vs normalize-rebase vs calibrate) I can queue them.
